text.p: Norway's Finansbanken ASA is to make a bid for specialist ship finance institution Skipskredittforeningen ASA, valuing the bank at around Norwegian crowns 250 million.
Finansbanken managing director Karl Moursund told Reuters the offer would be based on Skipskreditt's book value at the end of June, which he estimated at around 240-250 crowns per share.
The exact offer price will be based on Skipkreditt's interim results statement. Skipskreditt has one million shares in circulation.
The offer will open on August 11 and close on August 25, Finansbanken said.
Moursund said Finansbanken hopes to finance the acquisition through a new share issue to Skipskreditt shareholders.
Finansbanken said it has already received pledges to approve the offer from some 67 per cent of Skipskreditt shareholders and the backing of its board of directors.
However, it will only proceed with the offer if it receives approvals of over 90 percent.
Nedship Bank, a subsidary of Rabobank Nederland BA, acquired 70 percent of Skipskreditt's shipping loan portfolio at the end of last year.

Skipskreditt managing director Gunnar Foss said the moves reflected the increased pressure on small ship finance institutions that has stemmed from greater involvement in the sector by large financial institutions.
"It is increasingly difficult for a small institution to make a good return on its investments with the arrival of the larger banks in recent years. They have driven margins down," Foss said.

Moursund said: "Our interest in Skipskreditt has two elements. First it is to acquire a good brand name in Nowegian ship finance, and the second is to enlarge our own equity base through an issue of new shares."

Several other specialist Norwegian ship finance houses have been taken over in recent years. In 1993, MeesPierson of the Netherlands acquired Norsk Skibs Hypothekbank. Last year, Nedship acquired part of the Skipskreditt loan book, and Finansbanken took over Bergen-based Industri & Skipsbanken.
Skipskreditt has a current loan book of crowns 350 million, Finansbanken said.
Finansbanken had a total loan book of crowns 10.5 billion at the end of March, which included 27 percent with the shipping industry and 14 percent to the oil and offshore sector.
